title: A usable topic

blocks.heading: A usable topic
blocks.text: A good topic combines interest, relevance, ethical practice and a specific area and time. Test whether a manageable enquiry can answer it with available resources. Interest alone does not justify sensitive questions or unsafe fieldwork.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Interest
blocks.text: Interest gives a researcher a reason to sustain attention to an issue. It should not preselect the answer; record observations that challenge expectations as well as those that agree.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Relevance
blocks.text: Relevance links an enquiry to a meaningful development issue and the evidence needed. A water-journey question can inform access, while an unrelated opinion survey may not address that aim.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Ethics
blocks.text: Ethical enquiry respects consent, privacy, safety and participants’ choice not to take part. Use non-sensitive topics, explain purpose and avoid identifiable records where unnecessary. Do not pressure participants, enter unsafe sites or ask classmates for health or violence disclosures.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Specific scope
blocks.text: State the study area, population, variables and collection dates or period. A bounded question such as school-route travel time in one settlement during one week is more manageable than asking why education is unequal everywhere.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: Explain why a topic needs more than personal interest. It also needs safe feasible evidence and a bounded question; interest cannot make an intrusive or unanswerable enquiry suitable.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect the enquiry to its actual development topic and to Population (7.1) for denominators. Keep an individual record of the real procedure, changes, findings and limits. Fictional models teach the method and must not be presented as the learner’s completed fieldwork.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
